title: Observability Playbook — metrics, tracing & dashboard notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
Capture a pragmatic, incremental observability plan focused on: metrics definitions we need to ship in the next 6–8 weeks, lightweight tracing instrumentation for request flow through the stack, and a set of dashboards for on-call and product debugging. This is a working doc — lots of TODOs and open questions.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Redwood hosted + dedicated runtime surface (API gateway, router, serving runtime, cache), and the Console dashboards. Not covering infra provisioning metrics (cloud provider) except where they directly affect SLOs (e.g., node preemption).
- Audience: eng-observability, serving-runtime, platform-engineering, on-call SREs, product PMs (console)

Goals (prioritized):
1) Make user-facing latency and error behavior observable end-to-end.
2) Have apples-to-apples cost/per-token metrics tied to code paths and models.
3) Lightweight tracing to triage slow requests quickly (no heavy perf penalty).
4) Dashboards that support 5-min incident triage + 1h postmortem analysis.

High-level constraints / decisions:
- Default sampling: 1% global trace sample, 100% for errors (status >= 500) + 50% for requests > 1s. Evaluate overhead after two weeks.
- Metric cardinality: keep tag cardinality low. Model version and route are primary tags; avoid raw prompt/hash, obviously.
- Aggregation window: 1m counters and 1s histograms for latency percentiles where supported.

Core metric set (names are suggested canonical metric names):
- api.request.count: counter, unit=requests, tags=[env, route, model, outcome], description=Total incoming API requests. Used for throughput and error ratios. Owner: api-gateway. Alerts: sustained drop >50% vs baseline.

- api.request.errors: counter, unit=errors, tags=[env, route, model, error_class], description=Count of requests with non-2xx. Owner: api-gateway. Alert: error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m on high-traffic routes, >3% for low-traffic routes.

- api.request.latency.p50/p95/p99: histogram/quantiles, unit=ms, tags=[env, route, model], description=End-to-end request latency at the gateway. Owner: api-gateway. SLO target example: p95 < 600ms for small models, < 1s for larger ones (per route config).

- routing.queue.size: gauge, unit=items, tags=[env, pool], description=backlog of queued requests awaiting serving. Owner: router. Alert: queue.size > 100 for >5m.

- serving.inference.latency.p50/p95/p99: histogram, unit=ms, tags=[env, model, quantization, gpu_type], description=Actual model inference time (kernel execution + decode loop). Owner: serving-runtime. Use for isolating slow models or quantization regressions.

- serving.kvcache.hit_rate: gauge (0-1), tags=[env, model], description=Prefix/KV cache hit fraction. Impact: hit_rate directly reduces tokens executed. Owner: serving-runtime. Alert: drop >10% vs baseline.

- tokens.generated.count: counter, unit=tokens, tags=[env, model, route], description=Total tokens generated per model and route. Owner: serving-runtime. Used for cost reporting.

- gpu.utilization.percent: gauge, unit=percent, tags=[env, pool, gpu_type], description=GPU utilization to inform autoscale decisions. Owner: infra/cluster. Alert: sustained >85% for 10m = scale-up trigger.

- scheduler.batch.size.p50/p95: histogram, unit=items, tags=[env, pool], description=Batch sizes used by runtime batching. Suggested target: mean batch >= configured threshold during peak to control cost.

Metric naming guidelines (short):
- prefix by component: api.*, router.*, serving.*, infra.*
- use dot delimiters, no spaces, lowercase.
- prefer explicit tags (model, route) vs stuffing into metric name.

Tracing plan:
- Key spans per request: api.gateway.receive -> api.gateway.auth -> router.route-lookup -> router.enqueue -> scheduler.batching -> serving.infer -> serving.decode -> api.gateway.stream/send
- Trace attributes to capture (low-cardinality): request_id, route, model_name, model_version, pool_id, quantization, gpu_type, outcome (success/error_class), request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, start_timestamp_ms, end_timestamp_ms
- Sampling: as above. Error/janky sampling must be 100% for requests resulting in error codes >=500, or latency above route-specific thresholds.
- Baggage/Context: carry request_id and route only. Avoid user PII.
- Propagation: W3C traceparent for cross-service continuity.

Span-level instrumentation notes (implementers):
- serving.infer span should record: model.size (B), kvcache.hits, kvcache.lookups, compute_ms (time spent on device), host_ms (end-to-end server time inside runtime), decode_ms, tokens_produced.
- router.enqueue should record queue_position and estimated_wait_ms.
- scheduler.batch span should record batch_id and batch_size.

Dashboard sketches (required sets):
1) On-call Incident View (1 panel): top-line: global request rate, error rate, p95 latency (combined), active incidents flag. Drilldowns: errors by route, latency by route, recent traces (sampled) grouped by error class.
2) Serving Runtime Health (3 panels): per-pool GPU utilization, queue depth, batch size distribution, inference p95/p99.
3) Cost & Token Economics (2 panels): tokens per route/model, tokens per second, estimated $/hour by model (simple multiplies by instance-type token cost), kvcache hit rate trend.
4) Model Release Dashboard (for rollouts): compare new vs old model: request success rate, latency p95, token consumption, quality regression markers (if available).

Queries/implementation notes (Datadog/Grafana pseudo):
- p95 latency (api): quantile(0.95, api.request.latency{env:prod,route:payments}) 
- error rate by route: sum(api.request.errors{env:prod,route:*}) / sum(api.request.count{env:prod,route:*}) by route
- trace quicklist: show traces where span.duration > 2000ms or outcome:error_class:* ordered by duration

Alerting guidance (short):
- Keep alerts actionable and limited: rely on SLO burn alerts + resource saturations. Avoid noisy per-model p99 alerts without baseline.
- Immediate P0 alert: global error_rate > 3% for 5m AND total_request_rate > 1000rps.
- P1 alert: any pool gpu.utilization > 95% for 10m OR queue.size > 200 for 10m.
- SLO burn alerts: when error_budget < 25% and burn rate > 3x baseline.

Event instrumentation / metadata for postmortems:
- Always log: request_id, trace_id, route, model, model_version, pool_id, chosen_kernel_variant, error_class, sample_of_user_prompt_token_count (bounded). Logs should be structured JSON with the request_id for easy correlation.

Operational runbook snippets (for triage):
- Slow p95 on route X: check router.queue.size -> serving.inference.latency by model -> batch.size distribution -> recent traces for long decode spans.
- Increased cost for model Y: check tokens.generated.count vs baseline -> kvcache.hit_rate drop -> scheduler.batch.size change -> recent deploys (check rollout dashboard).

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Exact SLO numbers per route/model tier (need PM input).
- [ ] Sampling overhead experiment: enable 1% traces for 48h in prod and measure latency/CPU overhead.
- [ ] Confirm metric retention defaults across environments (prod 90d, staging 30d?).
- [ ] Decide on tracing backend (Jaeger vs Lightstep vs vendor). Initial lean preference: hosted OpenTelemetry collector -> Honeycomb for trace search.
- [ ] Standardize error_class taxonomy across components (auth, quota, model_timeout, model_error, infra).

Next steps (owners):
- Asha: finalize metric names and push proto instrumentation for api.gateway and router (2 weeks).
- Leo: prototype lightweight trace sampling and demo 1% overhead measurement (1 week).
- Maya: dashboard skeletons in Grafana with example queries (2 weeks).
- Tomas: add structured logging schema and a sample log forwarder config (1 week).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on sampling and cardinality. If you need more detail per model/version for a short time (release), we should plan targeted higher-sampling windows tied to rollout IDs.
- Keep feedback focused: missing metrics that block triage vs nice-to-have vanity metrics.

References and links:
- Tracing primer: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/
- Rollout dashboard proposal (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROLL-77
- Infra PR for trace headers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842

End of WIP playbook.
